Definition: apparently a primary word; a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation:--blade, grass, hay.
BiblicalUsage: Chortos is grass, the green herbage of the field, and Scripture uses it for provision and for the shortness of life. Jesus says the grass of the field, which today is and tomorrow is cast into the oven, is clothed by God, Peter says all flesh is as grass, and James says the rich man shall fade as the flower of the grass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the grass in these verses is both a promise and a warning, because God clothes it and it still fades. I hold that my life is as grass, and that is why I trust the God who clothes the grass and keeps it.
